title: A small cognitive core explains human behavior at scale
abstract: arXiv:2610.13603v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Psychology has proposed many principles of cognition. Each, however, was developed in isolation, leaving their combined explanatory power unknown. We assembled a small set of established principles into one model, which we call COntextual Retrieval and Encoding (CORE). CORE consists of a hierarchy of episodic memories into which prediction errors are written and whose encoding, retrieval, and forgetting depend on context. Fitted jointly to 7,036,442 choices from 137 experiments, the model predicts human choices better than black-box models and reproduces 75% of reported behavioral effects when simulated. Moreover, its latent variables show classic signatures of Bayesian learning and event segmentation. Taken together, these findings suggest that a small cognitive core accounts for much of human behavior. translated_title: 一个小型认知核心可大规模解释人类行为
translated_abstract: 心理学已经提出了许多认知原理。然而，每条原理都是在孤立状态下发展的，它们组合起来的解释力尚不清楚。我们将一小部分已确立的原理整合为一个模型，称之为情境检索与编码模型（COntextual Retrieval and Encoding，CORE）。CORE由一个情景记忆的层级结构组成，预测误差被写入其中，其编码、检索和遗忘均依赖于情境。该模型对来自137个实验的7,036,442个选择进行联合拟合后，对人类选择的预测优于黑箱模型，并且在模拟时能够再现75%的已报告行为效应。此外，其潜在变量呈现出贝叶斯学习和事件分割的经典特征。综合来看，这些发现表明一个小型认知核心即可解释人类行为的大部分，同时也通过在全部实验数据上构建计算模型，为使心理学超越各部分之和开辟了一条道路。
tldr: 该研究将多个经典认知原理整合为一个统一的计算模型CORE，其在超过700万个人类选择数据上拟合后不仅优于黑箱模型，还能再现75%的已报告行为效应，表明一个小型认知核心即可解释大部分人类行为。
en_tdlr: This study integrates established cognitive principles into a unified model called CORE, which, fitted to over 7 million human choices, outperforms black-box models and reproduces 75% of reported behavioral effects, suggesting that a small cognitive core explains much of human behavior.
